title: A path you drew shows you what you can do to it
goal: Everything you need to reshape a path is built and switched on, and none of it can be found. Draw a path and you are still holding the Pen, so the path shows no points at all; nothing says to switch tools, nothing says a double click bends a point, nothing says a double click on the line adds one, and nothing says Delete takes one out. A person who has just drawn a shape should be able to see and reach its points without being told.
notes:
Reported by the user on 2026-09-14, having just tried it: "the pen... i can't seem to do curves, select a point, I don't understand how to make circular, curved shapes, don't know how to delete a point, add a point, reposition a point".

Nothing is missing and nothing is broken. All of it is built and enabled: the user's dev app is on Next with next-pen and next-reshape-a-path both on by default, and Sources/Photonz/CanvasPathEdit.swift already implements drag to move, double click a point to convert between corner and smooth, double click a segment to insert, Shift click to extend the selection, Delete to remove picked points, arrow keys to nudge, and Option to break a lever. This is entirely a discoverability failure, so do not rebuild any of it.

THE CAUSE, and it is one line. CanvasPathEdit.swift:71, the editablePath property, requires `tool == .select`. The points only exist when the Select tool is in hand. Meanwhile a shipped task, 'the-pen-stays-in-your-hand-for-the-next-shape', deliberately leaves the PEN in your hand after a path is finished, so the moment a person finishes drawing they are in the one state where the path they just made shows nothing. Nothing on screen bridges those two facts. That is the whole report.

The file's own header says the intent was the opposite: "A path shows its points the moment it is picked, rather than hiding them behind a mode you have to know about." It does do that, but only for a tool the person is not holding yet.

Two honest options and the runner should weigh them rather than assume: show the points while the Pen is still in hand (which risks the Pen's own click-to-add-a-point gesture fighting the reshape gestures over the same pixels, so say how that is resolved), or hand back to Select once a path is finished the way other tools hand back, which contradicts the shipped stay-in-hand behaviour and so needs saying out loud. A third answer, saying it in the hint line, is weaker than both and should only win if it is argued for.

The second silent failure in the same check: `layer.transform.isIdentity`. Rotate a path and its points disappear with no explanation at all. Whatever else changes, that should say something.

The acceptance item about a first-time check is the one that matters most here. This feature passed a task whose acceptance already asked for gestures 'discoverable without reading anything', and it shipped undiscoverable, which means the check was not really made. Make it for real and write down what confused them.

Queue-driven app work targets the next release, and per CLAUDE.md a Current change is not finished until Next has it.
acceptance: After finishing a path with the Pen, the points of that path are reachable without the person knowing to change tools: either they show straight away, or the app says plainly what to do, and the audit says which was chosen and why
A path that is selected shows its points, its levers and which of them are picked, clearly enough to act on at a glance
Every one of these is discoverable without documentation: moving a point, bending it into a curve, adding a point, taking one out, and selecting more than one

The gestures that already exist keep working exactly as they do: drag a point, double click a point to convert it, double click a segment to add one, Shift click to extend the selection, Delete to remove, arrow keys to nudge, Option to break a lever
The pointer says what each thing under it does, the way every other handle on this canvas already does
A rotated path does not silently lose its points: today the check requires an identity transform, so a turned path shows nothing and says nothing. Either it reshapes, or it says why it cannot
A first-time check with somebody who has not seen this: they draw a shape and make one corner curved without being told anything, and whatever confused them is written down
Tested with the Pen still in hand and with Select in hand, because those are two different states and the second is the only one that works today
Audit under queue/audits/ with the path captured just after drawing and then with its points reachable, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Epic set to icon-vector by the 2026-09-15 manager pass: it was filed with the field blank, so it showed on the dashboard under no objective at all while sitting first in the p2 queue.

Adversarial review BEFORE building. Walked it as a first-timer: press P, click three corners, click the first one again. A shape lands, the Pen is still in hand, the chip goes back to 'Click to place a corner, or press and drag for a curve. Esc puts the Pen down.' Nothing on screen has changed about the shape that just appeared. The person's next thought is 'make that corner round', and there is no thread to pull: no dots, no cursor change, no sentence. That is exactly the report.

Weighed the three answers the task names.

(1) Hand back to Select after each path. Rejected. It reverses a shipped, deliberate decision ('the-pen-stays-in-your-hand-for-the-next-shape') that exists because an icon is five shapes in a row, and Illustrator/Figma/Sketch all keep the pen. Trading that away to fix a discoverability problem is paying with the wrong currency.

(2) Say it in the chip only. Rejected as the whole answer, kept as part of it. A chip that says 'press Escape first' is still a mode you have to be told about, and the file's own header says the intent was the opposite.

(3) Show the points while the Pen is in hand. Chosen. The collision the task warns about turns out to be already solved by the Pen's OWN vocabulary: the Pen already treats a press on an existing anchor as acting on that anchor rather than placing a fresh one (wouldClose on the first anchor, wouldFinish on the last), and it already draws a ring to say so. Extending that to the finished path's anchors is the same rule, not a new one.

Where the collision is resolved, precisely: a press on a POINT or a LEVER reshapes; a press anywhere else, INCLUDING on the outline, starts a new path exactly as today. The only thing lost is starting a new path within 8 screen points of a point of the path still picked, which is the smallest possible surface to give up. mouseDown routing already runs pathEditMouseDown before the pen branch, so this falls out of one condition.

What that costs, said out loud: double click the outline to add a point CANNOT work under the Pen, because the first of the two clicks starts a new path and lets the old one go before the second arrives. Four of the five gestures are live under the Pen (move, curve, remove, select more than one); adding a point stays a Select-tool gesture. The chip will name what is live rather than promising all five.

Shortest version that delivers the value: one condition in editablePath, two routing swaps so an in-flight anchor drag beats the pen branch, the pointer cue read above its tool==.select guard, and two new chip lines. No new gesture is invented.

Cut as decorative: nothing was added. Explicitly NOT building an Illustrator-style contextual pen (hover an anchor for minus, a segment for plus) - it would take away starting a new path anywhere near an existing one, which is a much bigger loss than the one above.

WHAT SHIPPED.

1. A picked path shows its points with the PEN in hand as well as Select (CanvasPathEdit.editablePath, one condition). Drag a point, drag a lever, double click a point to curve it, double click a lever to straighten one side, Option click a lever, Shift click to extend the selection, Delete to take points out, arrow keys to nudge: all live under the Pen. mouseDown already ran pathEditMouseDown before the pen branch, so only mouseDragged and mouseUp needed reordering, so an in-flight point drag beats the Pen instead of being handed to a session that never began.

2. The chip under the canvas is read path-first, pen-second (EditorView.canvas). That order is half the fix on its own: the Pen stays in hand after a shape lands, so the one chip on screen at the moment somebody wants to round a corner used to still be talking about placing the next anchor. The Pen's own line is never covered while it matters, because the first anchor of a new shape lets the last one go (penMouseDown), so no path is picked mid-draw.

3. A new line for that moment, PathEditHint.penOpening: 'Drag a point to reshape this shape. Double click a point to curve it. Click anywhere else to draw another.' It deliberately does NOT offer the outline double click, because the Pen cannot reach it (click one starts a new path and lets this one go before click two arrives). The last sentence is there because points appearing under a drawing tool reads like the tool changed under you.

4. The turned path now says why: PathEditHint.turned, 'This path is turned, so its points cannot be dragged. Set A back to 0 in Position & Size and they come back.' showsPathEditHint dropped its isIdentity requirement so the chip can carry it, and pathEditHintText reads the turned case in EditorState rather than from the canvas, because a turned path has no points and so the canvas has nothing to announce. 'Position & Size' is spelled the way LayerSection.geometry spells it, not 'Placement' as the task notes had it.

5. The pointer says what is under it under every tool that shows points, not just Select (CanvasPointerCue.pathPointCue, hoisted above the tool == .select gate). Side effect worth knowing: the path cue used to be read AFTER the canvas's own boundary handles, which is the opposite of the order mouseDown uses (pathEditMouseDown at line 89, canvas handles at line 238). It now matches.

6. New playtest step expectHint, with the path chip added to the harness's hint report in the editor's own stacking order. The chip was completely unclaimable before this: describe wrote it into the log and no walk read it back, which is how this feature shipped with every gesture working and the chip, at the one moment anybody needed it, talking about something else.

Flags: next-pen and next-reshape-a-path are both releases: [.next], so Current is untouched and the porting rule is satisfied by the gate rather than by a copy. Nothing moved into Releases/Next/.

VERIFICATION, and what could NOT be verified.

Verified: swift build clean, Scripts/test.sh green twice, 6882 tests in 552 suites, including new PhotonzCore tests for penOpening (it names dragging and double clicking and does NOT name the outline), for turned (it names the field that undoes it, spelled the way the panel spells it), for a picked point saying the same thing under either tool, and for the expectHint step refusing an empty claim.

NOT verified, and this is the honest gap: the Mac's screen was locked for the whole run, from before the first probe launch (Grants line: 'probe Screen Recording granted, screen locked') to the last check at 06:44 local. macOS stops drawing the window under a lock, so every walk reports status 'locked' and playtest.sh exits 3: not a pass and not a failure. queue/bin/sweep.sh status confirms the same thing from the loop's side, and a sweep is ALREADY pending for it, so I did not file another. So: no gesture in this change was driven in the real app, and no picture of it exists.

Scripts/playtest/path-points-under-the-pen-walk.json is written and has never run. It drives the whole feature: the Pen's own chip before drawing, the triangle landing with the Pen still in hand, the chip switching to the path's line, the pointer over a point, a point dragged with the Pen in hand (and still only two layers, so nothing was drawn by accident), the corner double clicked into a curve, Delete taking that point out, a press off the points still starting the next shape, and Select still adding a point on the outline. The pending sweep will run it; if it fails, that comes back as a task with the walk name in it.

I did NOT use PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1. My walk's claims are mostly document reads that would probably survive a lock, but the rule exists because a locked-screen run fooled runners on 2026-09-14, and a green result I could not trust is worse than no result.

Left rough, not filed (each is in the audit's rough list, where the user can react to it): starting a new path within about 8 screen points of a point of the path still picked now grabs the point instead, which is the deliberate cost of the change and the smallest surface it could have taken; adding a point stays a Select gesture because the Pen cannot reach a double click on the outline; a turned path still cannot be reshaped, it only explains itself now. The 'no pictures' finding was folded into the existing p1 task an-audit-gets-a-real-picture-of-the-app-again rather than filed as its near-twin.

The first-time check the acceptance asks for did not happen: it needs the app on screen. It is carried as the first two questions in the audit's evaluate list, which is the route by which a person's reaction becomes a task.
